<!-- Generated by Pixl from the skill "The five-line closing summary", version 1. Edit it in the Skills tab, not here: changes made here are overwritten. -->

## Steps
1. Run the tests as your last command.
2. End your last message with exactly five short plain lines and nothing after them. A review adds its VERDICT line after them.
3. Line 1 `Built:` what you built or changed.
4. Line 2 `How to open:` the command to run it, for example `./run.sh`, and the port (PORT, 8000 when not set).
5. Line 3 `Tested:` the real result you saw, for example `14 tests passed`, or `not run` and why.
6. Line 4 `Assumed:` what you decided alone, or `nothing`.
7. Line 5 `Next:` what the person should do, or `nothing`.
8. Plain words. No code, no headings, no bullets, at most 160 characters per line.
## Checklist
- [ ] Exactly five lines, in this order, each starting with its label.
- [ ] Tested holds a result you saw in this run.
## Definition of done
The last five lines of your message are the five labelled lines. The platform checks this and asks once more if they are wrong.
## Verify
Count the lines. Check each starts with Built, How to open, Tested, Assumed, Next.
## Common mistakes
- "All tests pass" without having run them.
- Six headings and a long report: the person reads five lines.
- Text after the five lines.
- Technical words the person cannot use.
## Example
Built: a page that greets you by name.
How to open: run ./run.sh and open the page on port 8000 of this computer.
Tested: 4 tests passed.
Assumed: names are plain text.
Next: nothing.
